learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the fundamental principles of economics, including scarcity, opportunity cost, and the four main factors required to produce anything!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Economics is the study of how people, businesses, and societies choose to use their limited resources to fulfill their unlimited wants and needs.
Human desires are endless, but the resources (like land, money, and time) to satisfy them are limited. Scarcity forces us to make choices.
When you make a choice, the 'opportunity cost' is the value of the next best alternative that you gave up. (e.g., If you study instead of playing, the fun of playing is your opportunity cost).
To produce any good or service, you need 4 things: Land (natural resources), Labour (human effort), Capital (tools, machines, money), and Enterprise (the entrepreneur who takes the risk).
Primary (agriculture/mining), Secondary (manufacturing/factories), and Tertiary (services like banking, teaching, and IT).

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ The Opportunity Cost Game
fun_activity.instructions: You have ₹500. You can either buy a movie ticket OR a new book. If you buy the book, what is your opportunity cost? Write down the experience you are giving up!

exam_tips: 📌 Always define Scarcity as the central problem of economics. Without scarcity, economics wouldn't exist!
📌 Memorize the four Factors of Production: Land, Labour, Capital, and Enterprise. Be ready to give examples of each.
📌 Differentiate between 'Physical Capital' (machines/tools) and 'Human Capital' (education/skills of people).
quick_recap: ⭐ Production is the creation of goods, and Consumption is using them up.
⭐ Microeconomics studies individual choices (one person or company), while Macroeconomics studies the whole country (inflation, unemployment).
⭐ Entrepreneurs are crucial because they combine the other three factors to create a business.
